Unavailable options are grey and cannot execute. B or releasing the opening controls closes it. No pages: all current options are on the wheel.
Strings.Exploration actions need one selected ch: Exploration actions need one selected character. Ground deployment opens Characters first; active ground and space combat open Actions first. LEFT stick click switches modes. Actor information never selects or moves the camera. Centring keeps it; another actor replaces it. Original cards are centred in the view at a stable readable size. Strings.Ground: 3 s in combat / 2 s in explorati: Ground: 3 s in combat / 2 s in exploration
Strings.Full right trigger 3 s on ground · move: Full right trigger 3 s on ground · move + head view
Strings.Hold the right trigger at least 95% down: Hold the right trigger at least 95% down over a valid destination: three seconds in Ground combat, two seconds in exploration. Once the original game accepts the move, enter the selected actor head view and remain there during movement. No extra move or action-point cost is added. Invalid paths, ability targeting, enemy turns and deployment cannot enter head view. A short click moves normally. B cancels the current action; B or zooming out leaves head view.
Strings.B always cancels the current interaction: B always cancels the current interaction: settings, wheel, native window or the game pending order. In gameplay it also leaves first-person view. The left menu button is Back/Cancel. Left trigger performs a secondary click. On the End turn wheel option, hold the opposite trigger for two seconds. No extra confirmation window appears. Pointing, A or a short click never ends the turn.
Strings.The same table gestures and LEFT-stick r: The same table gestures and LEFT-stick rotation/tilt apply, with ship-relative zoom. Battle entry frames our ship. Click orders without moving the camera; double-click frames the ship along its heading; full RIGHT trigger held for 2 s enters its view. LEFT wheel contains weapons, variants and ship-post abilities; click LEFT stick for the battle ships. RIGHT wheel contains native menus. A or the opposite trigger confirms abilities. On End turn, hold the opposite trigger for two seconds instead; no extra confirmation window appears. Native rules, resources and cooldowns remain authoritative.
Strings.Automatically use Minimal engine effects: Automatically use Minimal engine effects during ground and space combat, including preparation. Restore your selected effect level afterwards. Off by default. Keeps tactical indicators, particles and game rules. Does not change saved graphics settings.
Strings.Smoothly follow characters moved with th: Smoothly follow characters moved with the right stick. Forward, backward and sideways movement follow the right controller aiming direction at departure; turning your wrist steers. Camera follow cannot feed its rotation back into movement. Centre the stick to establish a new aiming reference. Off keeps the table still.
Exploration: move relative to right aim. Maps: pan.
Strings.In On-foot exploration, the right contro: In On-foot exploration, the right controller aim at departure defines forward, backward and sideways movement with the right stick. Turn your wrist to steer. Camera follow does not change that movement reference; centre the stick to establish a new one. HUD hover does not stop movement; clicks and open menus do. Navigation maps keep right-stick panning and left-stick zoom. Combat keeps native tactical pointer orders.
Strings.Waiting for a valid horizontal right-con: Waiting for a valid horizontal right-controller aim
Strings.Exploration actions need one selected ch: Exploration actions need one selected character. Ground deployment opens Characters first; inspecting a friendly portrait also selects it for placement. Active ground and space combat open Actions first. LEFT stick click switches modes. During the battle, inspection changes neither selection nor camera. Centring keeps the card; another actor replaces it. Original cards stay fixed inside the upper-left part of the HUD. Centre the RIGHT stick, then move it up or down to scroll. Release grip/trigger, press B or switch modes to close.
Strings.B cancels the current interaction: setti: B cancels the current interaction: settings, wheel, native window or pending order. In gameplay it also leaves first-person view. The left menu button is Back/Cancel; the left trigger performs a secondary click. On End turn, select with the LEFT stick or opposite Touch, then hold A or the opposite trigger for two seconds. Short clicks and release do not end the turn.
Strings.Table gestures and LEFT-stick rotation/t: Table gestures and LEFT-stick rotation/tilt use ship-relative zoom and keep the board level. Battle entry frames our ship. Click orders without moving the camera; double-click frames the ship along its heading; full RIGHT trigger held for 2 s enters its view. LEFT wheel contains weapons, variants and ship-post abilities; click LEFT stick for the battle ships. RIGHT wheel contains native menus. A or the opposite trigger confirms abilities. On End turn, select with the LEFT stick or opposite Touch, then hold A or the opposite trigger for two seconds. Native rules, resources and cooldowns remain authoritative.
Strings.Enable this independent optimization pac: Enable this independent optimization package at the next game launch. Each block can be disabled separately. Changes require restarting the game.
Strings.Shows applied blocks and saved changes p: Shows applied blocks and saved changes pending a game restart. A block with an incompatible native contract retains the original game path.
Strings.Independent blocks for combat and transi: Independent blocks for combat and transition performance. Every change requires a game restart. Timings and results depend on the scene.
Strings.HOLD A / opposite TRIGGER 2s · END TURN: HOLD A / opposite TRIGGER 2s · END TURN
Strings.During deployment, inspecting a friendly: During deployment, inspecting a friendly portrait also selects that character for placement. During the battle, inspection does not change selection or camera.
Strings.Reuse audited attack geometry inside the: Reuse audited attack geometry inside the same operation. Conditions, damage and random decisions remain native. Restart the game to apply changes.
Strings.Reuse unchanged movement calculations wi: Reuse unchanged movement calculations with invalidation when gameplay state changes. Restart the game to apply changes.
Strings.Reuse compatible native weapon action mo: Reuse compatible native weapon action models while refreshing the current weapons, abilities and availability. Restart the game to apply changes.
Strings.Avoid redundant native panel layout duri: Avoid redundant native panel layout during transitions, retaining original tutorial and window behaviour. Restart the game to apply changes.
Strings.Reuse audited effect component lists in: Reuse audited effect component lists in a bounded cache. Structural changes return to the native path. Restart the game to apply changes.
Strings.Avoid unchanged tactical geometry rebuil: Avoid unchanged tactical geometry rebuilds. Movement and attack indicators stay visible. Restart the game to apply changes.
Strings.Spread queued combat-history presentatio: Spread queued combat-history presentation across frames without dropping events or changing combat rules. Restart the game to apply changes.
Strings.Skip formatting AI diagnostics when the: Skip formatting AI diagnostics when the native logger would discard them. Enabled messages and errors remain available. Restart the game to apply changes.
Strings.Reuse participant enumeration within the: Reuse participant enumeration within the same initiative operation. Rebuild for the next operation so arrivals and departures stay current. Restart the game to apply changes.
Strings.Experimental: yield between audited AI e: Experimental: yield between audited AI evaluation iterations. Preserves candidates and resumes the decision; does not lower the game frame rate. Restart the game to apply changes.
Strings.Hold both triggers and both grips togeth: Hold both triggers and both grips together for 1 s to open or close settings. Release all four before repeating. A completed settings chord closes the wheel without executing its action. F1 also toggles settings and takes priority over game bindings.
Strings.LEFT stick / A / RIGHT trigger: hold 1 s: LEFT stick / A / RIGHT trigger: hold 1 s
Three independent ways to end the turn.
Strings.In Ground combat and Space combat, choos: In Ground combat and Space combat, choose End turn on the LEFT wheel. Keep the LEFT stick over its skull for 1 s, without any other confirmation. Alternatively, aim with the RIGHT skull and hold its trigger for 1 s, or hold A for 1 s on the selected option. Each method works alone. Releasing early cancels that hold; the action runs once. Holding all four grips/triggers instead opens settings.
Strings.Aim with LEFT stick / RIGHT skull + hold: Aim with LEFT stick / RIGHT skull + hold RIGHT grip
Strings.Hold RIGHT grip to read; release it to h: Hold RIGHT grip to read; release it to hide.
Strings.Choose a portrait with the LEFT stick or: Choose a portrait with the LEFT stick or point with the RIGHT skull, then hold the RIGHT grip to show its original card. This works for allies and enemies in Ground combat and for ships in Space combat. While gripping, the card stays fixed and another pointed portrait replaces it. Release the RIGHT grip, close the wheel or switch its mode to hide it. Inspecting during battle does not select or move the camera.
Strings.RIGHT grip: show card · RIGHT stick: scr: RIGHT grip: show card · RIGHT stick: scroll
Strings.Fixed native cards at the depth of the w: Fixed native cards at the depth of the wheels.
Strings.Every LEFT-wheel card uses the RIGHT gri: Every LEFT-wheel card uses the RIGHT grip: characters, ships, weapons and abilities. Point with the LEFT stick or RIGHT skull, then hold the RIGHT grip. Pointing or clicking alone does not open information. The card remains fixed while held, even if you centre the stick. Centre the RIGHT stick after opening, then move it up/down to scroll long content. Release the RIGHT grip to close.
Strings.Hold the LEFT grip and trigger. Move the: Hold the LEFT grip and trigger. Move the LEFT stick to the inner or outer ring, or point with the RIGHT skull. Hold the RIGHT grip for original information; release it to hide. A or the RIGHT trigger activates an available ability. With a card open, use A or a short trigger click; holding all four buttons for 1 s opens settings. Grey actions cannot run. Release the opening controls to close.
Strings.F1 toggles VR settings with priority ove: F1 toggles VR settings with priority over the game. Open this tutorial directly from Help · Touch controls on the main settings page or under Advanced settings. Choose a context and chapter without closing the guide. The welcome is offered once per launch, after the first playable load: YES opens the tutorial and NO continues playing.
Strings.Point with the RIGHT skull. One click se: Point with the RIGHT skull. One click selects or issues a native order without moving the camera. Double-click the same character, including an enemy, to frame it along its heading at the correct relative height. Ships use their equivalent framing. A also clicks. A deep hold only enters a controllable character or ship; map double-clicks keep their native function.
Strings.Battle entry frames our ship and keeps t: Battle entry frames our ship and keeps the board level sideways. Click ships or ground for native orders; double-click frames a ship along its heading. Hold the full RIGHT trigger 2 s over our ship for first person. The LEFT wheel alternates actions/ships; its weapon sectors match port, starboard and central mounts. RIGHT wheel opens menus. Original side/bottom HUD panels are hidden by default; Show space combat panels restores them in Advanced settings > Space.
Strings.Show the original ship panels. Hidden by: Show the original ship panels. Hidden by default: lower, left and right panels are replaced by the wheels. Opened windows and essential popups remain available.
Strings.HOLD LEFT STICK / A / RIGHT TRIGGER 1s ·: HOLD LEFT STICK / A / RIGHT TRIGGER 1s · END TURN
Entry frames our ship on a level board. Click for native orders; double-click frames a ship. Hold the full RIGHT trigger 2 s over our ship for first person. LEFT wheel: actions/ships, with weapons on their native side. RIGHT wheel: menus. Side/bottom panels are hidden; restore them in Advanced settings > Space.

Strings.Adjust text and buttons in tabletop mana: Adjust text and buttons in tabletop management windows. Native flat screens use Management window size and proportions instead. Dialogue HUD settings stay unchanged.
Strings.Enlarge the regular game HUD, including: Enlarge the regular game HUD, including its outer edges. 100% uses the binocular area; maximum 180%. Management windows have their own size setting. Text and button size changes content inside these edges.
Strings.Move the regular HUD left or right by up: Move the regular HUD left or right by up to 65% of its width. Management windows use their own horizontal position. Extreme values may place buttons outside your view. Aiming follows the displayed panel.
Strings.Move the regular HUD up or down by up to: Move the regular HUD up or down by up to 65% of its height. Negative moves down; positive moves up. Management windows use their own vertical position.
Strings.Show a discreet reminder of the controls: Show a discreet reminder of the controls available in the current context. Original game information remains visible.
Strings.In ground combat, double-click a movemen: In ground combat, double-click a movement destination with the right trigger to move and stay in first person. Native movement rules still apply. A single click keeps normal movement.
Strings.Restore the default interface or save th: Restore the default interface or save three layouts for HUD, management and both space maps. Eye resolution, DLSS, camera and controls stay unchanged.
Strings.Load saved HUD, management and space-map: Load saved HUD, management and space-map layouts. Other mod settings are preserved. Older presets keep any map or management settings they did not store.
Strings.Move management windows nearer or farthe: Move management windows nearer or farther without changing dialogue HUD placement or wheels.
Strings.Original keeps the game aspect ratio. Ma: Original keeps the game aspect ratio. Manual proportions reflow tabletop management windows; native flat screens change their displayed proportions. Aiming follows the displayed window.
Strings.Move management windows left or right in: Move management windows left or right independently of dialogue HUD placement and wheels.
Strings.Move management windows up or down indep: Move management windows up or down independently of dialogue HUD placement and wheels.
Strings.Fit inventory, equipment and management: Fit inventory, equipment and management windows inside your view. This size applies to complete windows, including native flat menus, independently of dialogue HUD settings and wheels.
Strings.Original keeps the game effects. Reduced: Original keeps the game effects. Reduced removes volumetric lighting/fog and screen-space reflections in VR. Minimal also removes ambient occlusion, bloom and camera blur. Keeps particles, tactical targeting and interface. Compare in the same scene; CPU stalls may remain.
Strings.Initially follows the game: Spanish if t: Initially follows the game: Spanish if the game uses Spanish, otherwise English. Your choice applies immediately to all mod menus, help and messages, is saved and takes priority on later launches. Original game text keeps its own language.
Strings.Open all mod settings, grouped as before: Open all mod settings, grouped as before. The image and language shortcuts share the same values as their advanced entries.
Strings.Adjust antialiasing, DLSS/DLAA, resoluti: Adjust antialiasing, DLSS/DLAA, resolution and sharpness while playing. The status below reports the mode actually in use.
Strings.TAA smooths edges using previous frames;: TAA smooths edges using previous frames; SMAA is non-temporal. DLAA works at full resolution; DLSS reconstructs from fewer pixels. Diagnostic tests NVIDIA while displaying TAA.
Strings.Final resolution sent to each eye. 100%: Final resolution sent to each eye. 100% uses the current VDXR recommendation. Higher values can reveal more detail and cost more GPU time. Changing resolution may briefly pause the image.
Strings.DLSS only. Lower values reduce GPU work: DLSS only. Lower values reduce GPU work and fine detail. Range: 50–100%, in 5% steps. DLAA always uses the full output resolution.
Strings.Sharpen edges without increasing resolut: Sharpen edges without increasing resolution. High values may create halos or grain. TAA and NVIDIA have separate values. TAA sharpening does not affect SMAA or No antialiasing.
Strings.Auto lets NVIDIA choose its model. K req: Auto lets NVIDIA choose its model. K requests that preset for DLSS/DLAA. This does not change resolution. The status distinguishes the request from the model that can be identified.
Strings.Recommended DLSS: 310.9.1.0. Other versi: Recommended DLSS: 310.9.1.0. Other versions and NVIDIA overrides are allowed. Version and source describe the runtime detected by NGX; unknown identity does not block it. TAA is retained on a real backend failure. Restart the game after replacing a DLL.
Limit how far the scene is drawn in VR. This can reduce slowdowns when looking across large areas. A short distance may hide the far background.
Strings.Choose the game default, 100, 60 or Cust: Choose the game default, 100, 60 or Custom. A shorter distance may improve frame rate and remove distant scenery. Locked during an automatic comparison.
Strings.Select Custom and set the range from 20: Select Custom and set the range from 20 to 400 scene units, in steps of 2. Reducing it may improve frame rate; check that scenery you need remains visible.
Strings.Adjust range using height, viewing direc: Adjust range using height, viewing direction and both eyes. Shortens it only when a reliable ground plane is found. Your manual ceiling returns at the horizon. Multi-level scenes may lose background; use Manual if this occurs.
Strings.Current range and manual ceiling in scen: Current range and manual ceiling in scene units. Adaptive range shortens gradually and expands immediately. Suspended during cinematics and automatic comparisons.
Strings.Adjust movement, rotation and zoom respo: Adjust movement, rotation and zoom response. The tabletop keeps its comfort limits. Recenter uses your current seated pose as the reference.
Strings.In third person, smoothly follow charact: In third person, smoothly follow characters moved with the right stick, with quicker alignment toward their travel direction. Off keeps the table still. Head view is unchanged. Movement keeps the heading at the start of each stick deflection; centre the stick to use the new heading.
Strings.Off by default. Enable left thumbrest to: Off by default. Enable left thumbrest touch + right stick up/down to change draw distance. When off, resting your thumb cannot change rendering range; the Draw distance menu remains available.
Strings.Adjust how far the tabletop moves when y: Adjust how far the tabletop moves when you move one or both hands while holding the grips. Physical hand and head tracking remain unchanged. Tracking jumps still have a speed limit.
Adjust tabletop rotation and tilt speed. 100% is the initial response; lower values move the view more slowly. Physical head tracking remains unchanged.
Strings.Adjust how much the tabletop scale chang: Adjust how much the tabletop scale changes as you move both hands together or apart while holding the grips. 100% is the initial response. Scale limits remain active.
Strings.Use your current headset position and or: Use your current headset position and orientation as the reference. Sit in your playing position, then press A or the right trigger.
Strings.Configure the game panel, indicators and: Configure the game panel, indicators and flat menu screen. These settings affect the game interface. This configuration panel is positioned separately.
Strings.Control the visibility of hands, gesture: Control the visibility of hands, gesture help and scene indicators.
Strings.Show servo-skull gesture hints near the: Show servo-skull gesture hints near the upper-right corner: movement, rotation, tilt, zoom and selection. Hiding the hints keeps the pointer and all controls.
Strings.Show a fully 3D servo-skull following ea: Show a fully 3D servo-skull following each hand. Rotate the Touch controllers to inspect it. Hiding the models keeps aiming available and lets you compare their rendering cost.
Strings.Place unit indicators above their charac: Place unit indicators above their characters in the 3D scene. Off returns these indicators to the flat game panel.
Strings.Limit the extra marker enlargement used: Limit the extra marker enlargement used to retain legibility as tabletop scale changes. 1.0 removes this extra enlargement; higher values allow larger markers.
Strings.The keyboard-and-mouse interface adapts: The keyboard-and-mouse interface adapts its windows to the headset aspect ratio. Adjust size, aspect and position without restarting.
Strings.Use the wheels in exploration and combat: Use the wheels in exploration and combat. Hides the usual party, action and menu bars while retaining dialogues, tutorials and opened windows. Turn off to restore the original panels or compare their cost.
Strings.Set text and button size in the enlarged: Set text and button size in the enlarged inventory, map and other service windows. These windows stay centred and provide CLOSE below. Regular HUD placement is preserved when they close.
Strings.Enlarge the HUD content from 100% to 180: Enlarge the HUD content from 100% to 180% inside the same panel area. Reflows the keyboard-and-mouse layout instead of pushing its edges farther apart. Applies immediately; very large values can crowd fixed-size game windows. Does not lower interface resolution or move world/map markers.
Strings.Show or hide the game interface inside t: Show or hide the game interface inside the tabletop. This configuration panel remains available so you can turn it back on.
Strings.Move the game panel nearer to or farther: Move the game panel nearer to or farther from your head, in virtual metres. Does not reposition this configuration panel.
Strings.Enlarge the whole interface, including i: Enlarge the whole interface, including its outer edges. 100% uses the centred binocular area; maximum 180%. To make text and buttons larger while keeping these edges in place, use Text and button size instead. Also affects flat menus.
Strings.Headset adapts the interface to the bino: Headset adapts the interface to the binocular field of view. Manual values change width-to-height ratio without stretching text. Affects the tabletop HUD; flat menus keep the original window ratio.
Strings.Move the interface and flat menus by up: Move the interface and flat menus by up to 65% of their width. Size is preserved. Extreme values may place buttons outside your view. Aiming follows the actual panel position.
Move the interface and flat menus by up to 65% of their height without shrinking them. Negative moves down; positive moves up. Extreme values may leave elements outside your view.
Strings.Actual pixels for flat menus and the ind: Actual pixels for flat menus and the independent HUD. Does not change text size or eye resolution. Higher values may improve clarity and cost GPU time. Changing the window may briefly pause the image. Actual shows the applied size.
Strings.Render the PC panel and world unit indic: Render the PC panel and world unit indicators at a resolution independent of DLSS. Preserves masks, drawing order and aiming. Turn off to compare with the earlier path, whose clarity depends on each eye internal resolution.
Strings.Show the game on a flat screen when a fu: Show the game on a flat screen when a full-screen menu suspends the tabletop. Touch pointing remains available in those menus.
Strings.Mod options that reduce rendering work a: Mod options that reduce rendering work and record timings. Their effect depends on the scene and active effects. Compare while holding the same view.
Strings.Avoid repeatedly updating every panel wh: Avoid repeatedly updating every panel when a popup tries several consecutive positions. Keeps an update per popup. Turn off to compare with the previous path.
Strings.Keep panel geometry fixed while moving y: Keep panel geometry fixed while moving your head or zooming the table. Reduces repeated Canvas work without lowering HUD resolution. Turn off for a live comparison; maps keep their registered projection.
Strings.Update each unit indicator separately. M: Update each unit indicator separately. May reduce CPU work but increase draw calls and pointing cost. Off by default. Compare in the same combat view.
Strings.Reuse one eye image for the monitor inst: Reuse one eye image for the monitor instead of drawing the world again. Can reduce work in VR. Both eyes continue to render separately.
Strings.Allow the game FSR setting to affect bot: Allow the game FSR setting to affect both eyes. May reduce detail to save GPU time. Suspended while DLSS, DLAA or NVIDIA Diagnostic is active.
Strings.Reduce drawing outside the visible heads: Reduce drawing outside the visible headset area. A margin is preserved. Culling may be suspended when effects such as reflections need those regions.
Strings.Cull repeated objects drawn by the GPU o: Cull repeated objects drawn by the GPU outside the view. May reduce rendering work. Suspended when effects or viewing direction require the full image.
Strings.Update which effects the VR view needs w: Update which effects the VR view needs when monitor rendering is reduced. Considers both eyes rather than relying on a camera that is no longer drawn.
Strings.Start or pause timing collection and dia: Start or pause timing collection and diagnostic file writing. Turn off to compare its overhead. Error messages remain available and existing files are preserved.
Strings.Add rendering, logic, camera and interfa: Add rendering, logic, camera and interface timings to identify spikes. Active only while diagnostics are recording. Adds measurement overhead.
Strings.Clear recent frame-rate and timing sampl: Clear recent frame-rate and timing samples to begin a fresh comparison. Quality settings and previously saved diagnostic files are preserved.
Strings.Adjust grids, unit markers and character: Adjust grids, unit markers and character highlights throughout the VR scene, in exploration and combat. Preserves the game's information and rules.

Strings.Hold both triggers and both grips togeth: Hold both triggers and both grips together for 2 s to open or close settings. Release all four before repeating. Strings.Point at a row or button and release A o: Point at a row or button and release A or the RIGHT trigger over it to activate. Release both before confirming again. Strings.F1 opens/closes the mod settings and tak: F1 opens/closes the mod settings and takes priority over the game binding. Holding it only acts once. Strings.Hidden at launch. Available in explorati: Hidden at launch. Available in exploration and both combats.
